changes.before: If the instant is 12:30 UTC the same day, what two dates print?
changes.after: Show the same moment as a local date in two time zones.

before:
Instant represents a point on the time line. A ZoneId supplies rules for presenting that point as a local date and time. LocalDate alone contains no zone or time-of-day.

Instant.parse(text) parses an ISO-8601 instant such as the supplied UTC text ending in Z. Calling toLocalDate() on the zoned result extracts its calendar date; that LocalDate does not retain the time-of-day or zone.

At 00:30 UTC on January 1, New York is still on December 31. Converting the instant with atZone preserves the instant, not the displayed calendar date. Region zones carry daylight-saving rules; fixed UTC does not shift seasonally.

Expected output or behavior: 2025-01-01
2024-12-31. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why a birthday can be a LocalDate while an event timestamp needs an instant and display zone. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Instant represents one moment on the timeline. Instant.parse reads it from standard date-and-time text; the ending Z means UTC, a worldwide time reference. LocalDate holds only a calendar date, without a time or time zone.

ZoneId selects the rules for a place's local time. atZone applies those rules without changing the moment itself. Region rules can include daylight saving changes. toLocalDate then keeps only the calendar date shown in that zone.
The program prints 2025-01-01, then 2024-12-31. At half past midnight in UTC, New York is still on the previous evening.
The quiz moves the instant to half past noon UTC that day. Subtract the same five hours to find New York's local date.

before.question: If the instant is 12:30 UTC the same day, what two dates print?
choices: The zone changes the underlying instant.
before.explanation: At that later instant New York has also reached January 1.

after.question: Use 12:30 UTC on January 1 instead. Which two dates print?
choices: The zone changes the instant instead of its displayed date
after.explanation: At 12:30 UTC, New York is at 07:30 on January 1. Both displayed dates are now January 1.
